shortName: University of Iowa Roy J. and Lucille A. Carver College of Medicine
additionalCoursework:
We accept community college coursework. We accept online coursework from accredited universities. AP/CLEP coursework may satisfy course requirements if listed on a college transcript. Applicants may apply while in the process of completing pre-requisite coursework. However, we recommend that applicants complete all required science coursework before they submit an application.
In programs where premedical science courses are offered on either a graded or pass/fail basis, we strongly recommend that you take those courses for a grade.

medSchoolStudLife.diversity: The Office of Education Support advances the educational mission by providing professional development and academic programming for all students. Through intentional skill development and coordinated support, the office empowers future healthcare professionals to excel while meeting the needs of their communities. The Office strengthens alignment among undergraduate medical education (UME), graduate medical education (GME) and continuing medical education (CME). It also partners closely with UI pre-health advisors to encourage matriculation into CCOM while expanding pathways for Iowa’s pre-health students by addressing opportunity gaps, strengthening mentorship, and enhancing academic preparation across institutions statewide.  As the coordinating office for CCOM’s educational mission, it streamlines communication, supports student organizations, and maintains a standardized education dashboard to promote transparency, alignment, and continuous improvement across the enterprise.
medSchoolStudLife.leaveOfAbsence: Leaves of absence are generally limited to one year and must be approved in advance after meeting with a dean of student affairs or the registrar.  If the student is not in good academic standing, requests may be reviewed by the Student Promotions Committee.
medSchoolStudLife.organizationActivities: There are a wide variety of student organizations at the Carver College of Medicine; including student government, specialty interest groups, community health outreach, intramural sports and political interest. A list can be found here: https://medicine.uiowa.edu/md/student-support/opportunities-growth/student-organizations . Creating new interest groups is simple and students are encouraged to do so!
medSchoolStudLife.setting: The college is on the 1,900-acre campus of a major research institution, the University of Iowa, and includes one of the largest university-owned teaching hospitals. Iowa City is a community of 78,000 with local public transportation to the college.  Cultural activities, Big 10 sports, shopping, and nearby parks provide outlets for recreation and services.
medSchoolStudLife.housing: On-campus housing is generally not available. The university offers a clearinghouse to help students find housing. Typical two-bedroom apartments range from $500 (shared)-$1200/month. There are two co-ed medical societies ranging from $300-500/month. Affordable housing can be found within walking or biking distance, on campus and off campus. There are two inexpensive city bus routes, as well as the free UI campus buses that service our main medical school building throughout the day and night.
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystems: EQUAL Meds is an active student group with strong support from the administration, faculty, staff, and students. EQUAL Meds mission is to educate our community on health issues that pertain to lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender, queer, and/or questioning (LGBTQ) patients and to provide a support network for LGBTQ health professional students.   EQUAL Meds also provides a forum where LGBTQ identified students can interact with other graduate and students as well as with faculty and staff from the larger University of Iowa Health Care community.  EQUAL Meds sponsors social gatherings with opportunities for networking, mentoring, and creating community. OutList is a voluntary and public webpage that lists LGBTQ+ identified community members’ names, affiliations, and e-mail addresses.  Additionally, there is an option to list specific gender identity, sexual identity, and/or pronouns.  The community members may include faculty, staff, residents, fellows, post docs, and/or students.
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystemsForDisabilities: The student organization, Medical Students with Disability and Chronic Illness at Iowa, is an active group supporting many students. The Medical Student Counseling Center provides resources and programs for learners with disabilities: https://md.medicine.uiowa.edu/student-and-program-resources/student-counseling
medSchoolStudLife.wellnessPrograms:
Every MD student has access to a free Medical Student Counseling Center. This office has four trained counselors offering: personal counseling, disability accommodations, academic support with free tutoring, career development, and a variety of wellness programs and resources. Please visit for more detailed office information: https://medicine.uiowa.edu/md/student-support/student-counseling

There is also a Student Wellness Organization for MD students. Founded in 2020, the Student Wellness Organization’s mission is to provide a centralized place for students passionate about student wellness to collaborate on activities and projects meant to improve student wellness at the Carver College of Medicine.
medSchoolStudLife.campusCulture: The Carver College of Medicine is a part of The University of Iowa, located in Iowa City, IA. The University of Iowa is a Big 10 Institution, and the culture is vibrant, diverse, and has many "big city amenities" located in a smaller community of about 100,000.  Iowa Health Care is the largest system in the state.
medSchoolStudLife.transportationAdditionalInfo: There is one family medicine rotation in which the use of a car to travel to the site is preferable.

medSchoolCurriculum.dressCode: Students are expected to dress appropriately and to conduct themselves in a manner consistent with the location and nature of their educational activities.
medSchoolCurriculum.tutoringPrograms: Office hours are generally 8-5, but Financial Aid and the Counseling Center, which provides tutoring, offer extended hours.
medSchoolCurriculum.patientInteraction: First semester in Early Clinical Experiences.
medSchoolCurriculum.instructionStyle: Case-based, including small groups and some lectures
medSchoolCurriculum.clinicalRotations: Clerkships begin in January of 2nd year.
medSchoolCurriculum.prematriculationProgram: A Prematriculation Program, Introduction to Medical Education at Iowa (IMEI), is an 8 week program offered to admitted students only.  Also, summer research fellowship is available.
medSchoolCurriculum.curricularHighlights:
Innovation, Integration and Individualization constitute the 'Three I’s' of our New Horizons Curriculum. Given the phenomenal pace of change in technologic progress and the explosion of scientific discovery of new knowledge, tomorrow’s physicians must now be educated in ways that will allow them to continuously adapt to the complex and continuously evolving environment of health care delivery.  The goal of the new curriculum is to develop enduring attitudes, skills, and knowledge that will provide focus and direction for tomorrow’s physicians in a future that cannot be easily predicted.

Students are fully integrated into the clinical setting by the M2 second semester, providing more time to tailor their educational experience. Pre clinical curriculum is shared with 25 PA students. UI medical students have earned impressive scores on the USMLE and successfully matched with top-quality residency programs.
medSchoolCurriculum.primaryCarePrograms: CCOM is proud of its record of sustained commitment to primary care.  It is believed that early and sustained exposure of medical students to primary care and primary care physicians consistently results in the CCOM being one of the nation's top producers of primary care physicians.  In addition to a required four-week preceptorship in Family Medicine, students spend another four weeks on a Community Based Primary Care rotation and four weeks of an Outpatient Internal Medicine rotation.  The Carver Rural Iowa Scholars Program (CRISP) provides four students each year with training and financial support.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchPrograms: The research enterprise of the University of Iowa Carver College of Medicine garnered over $266.4 million in external research funding in FY25. According to the 2025 edition of U.S. News & World Report’s “Best Graduate Schools,” research in the UI Carver College of Medicine is ranked Tier 2 (top 50) nationally. Additionally, NIH funding ranks 46th overall, according to the Blue Ridge Institute for Medical Research. Many faculty members are internationally renowned for their research. Ten faculty are members of the National Academy of Medicine, and three are members of the National Academies of Sciences. 80-100 CCOM PM1 and M1 students participate in full-time summer research under the guidance of these experienced physician-scientist mentors.
medSchoolCurriculum.communityServiceText: Mobile Clinic is a student organization providing free health screening, prevention, education, and basic services to underserved and uninsured populations throughout the state of Iowa.
medSchoolCurriculum.affiliatedHospitals: Medical students complete the majority of their training at the University of Iowa Hospitals & Clinics and VA Hospital in Iowa City. Clinical training is also at The Des Moines campus.
medSchoolCurriculum.gradingSystem: Honors; Near Honors; Pass; and Fail.  Clinical & Professions Skills (1-3) and Medicine & Society (1-3) in the pre-clinical curriculum are Pass/Fail only.

medSchoolInformation.generalInformation:
Iowa Health Care offers the right combination for dynamic medical education. Whether it is our 800-bed main campus hospital complex in Iowa City, our world-class pediatric hospital right next door, or one of our dozens of offsite locations throughout  the state of Iowa. Our medical students do the majority of their clinical experiences at the University of Iowa Hospitals and Clinics, which is connected by skywalk to the building for the majority of M1 classes. 

The college is part of a major health center serving the state and region. The health sciences campus includes the University of Iowa Hospitals and Clinics; Veterans Affairs Hospital; Hardin Health Sciences Library; Medical Education and Research Facility and basic sciences, dental, nursing, and pharmacy buildings. Because of the robust health sciences offerings here, inter-professional education is an integral part of medical student learning.
medSchoolInformation.missionStatement:
The Admissions Committee for the University of Iowa Roy J. and Lucille A. Carver College of Medicine admits students who have a genuine interest in the study and practice of medicine; show a desire and commitment to serve the public in matters of health; and who have the personal, professional and intellectual skills and characteristics required to become and competent and caring physician. 

Personal qualities considered by the Admissions Committee include high moral character, independent thinking, the ability to communicate and interact with others in a sensitive and caring way, the ability to maintain professionalism in stressful situations, and dedication to the idea of service.

Understanding the importance of the educational benefits resulting from a diverse student population and the interest by the medical profession in serving the healthcare needs of a changing American population, the Admissions Committee values each applicant’s unique strengths, experiences and background.

To execute our mission, the committee utilizes a holistic review of all candidates. Our committee values each candidates' different experiences and personal stories and takes into consideration: first generation college students, rural backgrounds and experiences, socioeconomic status, and any other impactful experiences students describe in their application that will make them a compassionate and excellent physician.

Please read our sections about Campus Life to learn more about how Carver's mission informs our culture of collaboration and other initiatives.

medSchoolApplication.applicantResponseToOffer: Two weeks from date of letter of acceptance.
medSchoolApplication.letterGuidance: Our committee encourages applicants to pick letter writers that know the applicant well. Academic letter writers do not need to be within the student's major or know the student from a science course -applicants should choose the letter writers that know them well.
medSchoolApplication.typicalInterviewDay:
Carver conducts "closed file" interviews -  interviewers are faculty volunteers and want to get to know candidates "off of paper" completely!  Do not let this scare you - candidates often tell us how nervous they were before the interview and feel very positive about it afterwards. We make great efforts to keep nerves low so candidates can perform at their very best on interview day. 

A previous interviewee wrote this about their Carver interview experience: "I think the interview process was amazing! This was my first in -person interview experience, and it was a lot less stressful than I imagined."

We offer both in person and virtual interviews. Admissions committee members will not know the format candidates choose. 

For more information, see https://md.medicine.uiowa.edu/admissions/application-process/interview-faq
medSchoolApplication.interviewFormat: Candidates are interviewed individually by two faculty members for 25 minutes.  The interview day includes a case-based learning session facilitated by M4 students. Both virtual and in person interview formats are available.
medSchoolApplication.videoInterview: Video interviews are not offered. Virtual interviews are offered.
medSchoolApplication.secApplSentTo: Overall and BCPM GPA 3.0. If not 3.0,  20 hours science post bacc or graduate work at 3.5 or higher. MCAT score must be 500 or higher to receive a secondary (all subcategories at least 123).
medSchoolApplication.secApplLatestDtText: December 15, 2026 Secondary application submission deadline (Oct 15 is strongly encouraged)
medSchoolApplication.ctsRequired: There is no required relationship to Carver or the state of Iowa for non-resident applicants.
medSchoolApplication.additionalInfo:
The Roy J. and Lucille A. Carver College of Medicine seeks qualified students who exemplify the interests, commitment to serve, and intellectual and conceptual skills that our college instills in all its faculty, staff, and students. The Admissions Committee values each individual’s unique experiences, strengths, and background. 

Candidates are reviewed holistically by a 30 member admissions committee comprised of faculty, current students, and  one community physician. Our admissions staff understands the stressors of the medical school application process, and thus tries to be as transparent and approachable as possible. We welcome questions from prospective applicants!
medSchoolApplication.mcatScoresAdditionalInfo: The last three years of MCAT scores are visible to the admissions committee. The most recent score determines the eligibility of a secondary application.
medSchoolApplication.mcatScreenAdditionalInfo: Applicants' most recent score must be 500 or greater to receive a secondary application. A subsection total of 123 must be attained on each section.
medSchoolApplication.gpaScreenAdditionalInfo: Applicants must have achieved an overall and science* grade-point average of 3.0 or higher (on a 4.0 scale) for all undergraduate college work. Applicants who have not achieved the former must have completed a minimum of 20 hours of science postbaccalaureate or graduate work at 3.5 or higher. In programs where premedical science courses are offered on either a graded or pass/fail basis, we strongly recommend that you take those courses for a grade.
medSchoolApplication.minCreditHourInfo: Applicants who have not achieved the former must have completed a minimum of 20 hours of science postbaccalaureate or graduate work at 3.5 or higher. Courses do not expire.
medSchoolApplication.courseworkAcceptanceInfo: Coursework taken at community colleges is acceptable for introductory/prerequisite coursework.  Our admissions committee generally prefers upper level science courses taken at a university level.
medSchoolApplication.letterOfIntentAdditionalInfo:
Our committee does not accept letters of intent.

Applicants can provide up to 3 additional updates for the committee in free and open text directly in the secondary application, "additional updates" section.
medSchoolApplication.technicalStandardInfo: Applicants for admissions to the Carver College of Medicine and continuing students must possess the capability to complete the entire medical curriculum (basic and clinical sciences, as well as professional skills) and achieve the degree. To this end, all courses in the curriculum must be completed successfully. In order to acquire the knowledge and skills to function in a broad variety of clinical situations and to render a wide spectrum of patient care, candidates for the M.D. degree must have abilities and skills in the following six Technical Standards categories: Observation, Communication, Motor skills, Intellectual, Conceptual, Integrative and Quantitative Abilities, Behavioral and Social Attributes, and Cultural Competency.

medSchoolFinancial.financialAid: Applicants are selected without consideration of their financial resources or ability to meet the cost of medical school. CCOM financial aid staff actively seek sources so every student interested can finance their education. Students receive financial aid based on calculations from their FAFSA application.  Scholarship and grant assistance is available but the majority of financial aid is loans;  loans from private, collegiate and federal sources are available. CCOM maintains its own Financial Services Department which handles awarding of financial aid and financial awareness counseling.

medSchoolSelection.premedReqRec:
Our curriculum requires at least one semester of Biochemistry.  It may be taken to fulfill either the Chemistry requirement (minimum of 2 yrs to included general and organic, both with labs, and biochemistry) or the Advanced Biology requirement (1 semester) if have 2 yrs of general and organic chemistry.  Recommended advanced biology courses include molecular & cell biology, human physiology, genetics or microbiology. 

Other recommended, though not required courses include: psychology, sociology, languages, and other non-science, writing intensive courses.
medSchoolSelection.medSchoolMediaSites: Facebook sites: Discover Carver College of Medicine, Diversity University of Iowa Carver College of Medicine
medSchoolSelection.selectionFactors: The Admissions Committee selects applicants best qualified for the study and practice of medicine. Applicants must have a Bachelor's degree obtained in residence with at least a 3.0 GPA (based on a 4.0 scale) for undergraduate work undertaken, unless there is significant (at least 3.5 on 20 hrs) science work in a postbaccaulareate or graduate program. Factors considered: overall academic record; science GPA; MCAT scores; medical experiences; personal characteristics (evaluated through letters of recommendation, information on the AMCAS application, and information on the supplemental form); personal interview; residency (preference given to Iowa residents that meet the missions of Carver. Consideration also given to outstanding non-residents).
medSchoolSelection.preMedShadowText: Physician shadowing is highly recommended.  Insight into the learning experience and impact on the applicant are considered. We encourage applicants to shadow a wide variety of different kinds of physicians.
